entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 29 Is 29:1-24 . Coming Invasion of Jerusalem: Its Failure: Unbelief of the Jews. This chapter opens the series of prophecies as to the invasion of Judea under Sennacherib, and its deliverance. 1. Ariel-- Jerusalem; Ariel means "Lion of God," that is, city rendered by God invincible: the lion is emblem of a mighty hero ( 2Sa 23:20 ). Otherwise "Hearth of God," that is, place where the altar-fire continually burns to God ( Is 31:9 ; Eze 43:15 , 16 ). add ... year to year-- ironically; suffer one year after another to glide on in the round of formal, heartless "sacrifices." Rather, "add yet another year" to the one just closed [Maurer]. Let a year elapse and a little more ( Is 32:10 , Margin). let ... kill sacrifices-- rather, "let the beasts (of another year) go round" [Maurer]; that is, after the completion of a year "I will distress Ariel."

Yet--</hi>rather, "Then."<div eID="gen14724" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14725" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heaviness ... sorrow--</hi>rather, preserving the Hebrew paronomasia, "groaning" and "moaning."<div eID="gen14725" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14726" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as Ariel--</hi>either, "the city shall be as a lion of God," that is, it shall emerge from its dangers unvanquished; or "it shall be as the altar of burnt offering," consuming with fire the besiegers (<reference osisRef="Isa.29.6">Is 29:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.30.30">Is 30:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.31.9">31:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.10.2">Le 10:2</reference>); or best, as <reference osisRef="Isa.29.3">Is 29:3</reference> continues the threat, and the promise of deliverance does not come till <reference osisRef="Isa.29.4">Is 29:4</reference>, "it shall be like a hearth of burning," that is, a scene of devastation by fire [G. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8833"/><div sID="gen14731" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8833"/>4. Jerusalem shall be as a captive, humbled to the dust. Her voice shall come from the earth as that of the spirit-charmers or necromancers (<reference osisRef="Isa.8.19">Is 8:19</reference>), faint and shrill, as the voice of the dead was supposed to be. Ventriloquism was doubtless the trick caused to make the voice appear to come from the earth (<reference osisRef="Isa.19.3">Is 19:3</reference>). An appropriate retribution that Jerusalem, which consulted necromancers, should be made like them! <div eID="gen14731" type="x-p"/>

Jehovah gives them up judicially to their own hardness of heart (compare <reference osisRef="Zech.14.13">Zec 14:13</reference>). Quoted by Paul, with variations from the Septuagint, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.8">Ro 11:8</reference>. See <reference osisRef="Isa.6.10">Is 6:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.69.23">Psa 69:23</reference>.<div eID="gen14746" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14747" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eyes; the prophets, &c.--</hi>rather, "hath closed your eyes, the prophets; and your heads (Margin; see also <reference osisRef="Isa.3.2">Is 3:2</reference>), the seers, He hath covered." The Orientals cover the head to sleep; thus "covered" is parallel to "closed your eyes" (<reference osisRef="Judg.4.19">Jud 4:19</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8843"/><div sID="gen14752" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8843"/>14. (<reference osisRef="Hab.1.5">Ha 1:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.41">Ac 13:41</reference>). The "marvellous work" is one of unparalleled vengeance on the hypocrites: compare "strange work," <reference osisRef="Isa.28.21">Is 28:21</reference>.
